text:
alex: heads-up — observed a P99 tail spike (2.8x) on inference nodes after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. Correlates with KV 'aging sweep' kicking in under sustained long-context workloads.

maria: oh no, which cluster/commit?

alex: can repro on hh-prod-sim (commit d4c3f). happens when avg seq_len > 2048 and request Q depth > 120. spike aligns with a periodic slab sweep event.

sam: any heap growth visible? sounds like fragmentation -> paging.

alex: yes, RSS jumps ~300MB for a minute, then comes down. but latency stays elevated for ~30-60s. heap profiler snapshot: 

```
# kv arena stats
active_pages: 1240
free_pages: 80
fragmentation_pct: 22.7
evict_ops/sec: 540 -> 1200 during spike
pager_io_ops: 480/s
```

maria: interesting — eviction_ops doubled. policy was LRU on that pool, right?

alex: yes kv.eviction_policy=LRU. we swapped kernel selection to prefer fused-attn kernel around same deploy, but not sure how they interact.

perf-bot: profile summary attached: cpu: spikes in `evicter::sweep` and `kv::reinsert`, syscalls show increased page faults. flamegraph link: https://perf/reports/1729876543

sam: LRU under sustained hotset churn can cause reinsert storms if reinsert moves entries to MRU and another concurrent sweep evicts them again -> oscillation. FIFO behaves differently (less churn) but has correctness tradeoffs for reuse.

maria: could be a race where reinserts are not updating slab metadata atomically, so reinserted pages get counted as new and immediately aged out. need to check handoff ordering.

alex: I captured a minimal repro script (local hh-sim) — runs many long-context requests, then waits for the sweep interval to start.

```
# repro (approx)
for i in `seq 1 200`; do 
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"context_len":2500,"batch":1}' &
done
sleep 20
# observe p99 with `rtt` tool
```

sam: quick mitigation: increase `kv.aging_sweep_interval_ms` from 5000 -> 15000 and reduce `evicter.max_batch_size` to cut thrash. That should reduce overlap of sweeps and reinserts.

maria: agree, but we should also add a fast-path: if reinserting an item that was evicted < X ms ago, mark as 'recent' and place it near tail instead of MRU to avoid immediate re-evict.

alex: tested the interval tweak in hh-sim — P99 improved ~30%, RSS spike reduced. but still a small tail blip.

perf-bot: comparison metrics:
- baseline (pre-change): p99=42ms, rss_p50=1.8GB
- after kernel-select change + LRU: p99=118ms, rss_p50=2.1GB
- interval tweak: p99=82ms, rss_p50=1.95GB

sam: long-term fix items:
- add atomic reinsertion handshake (prevent concurrent sweep from treating it as new)
- instrument per-slab timestamps for last-evicted -> allow short TTL where reinsert goes to cold tail
- run LRU vs FIFO microbench under hh-long-context profile to quantify tradeoffs

maria: also check batching heuristics: fused kernel decreased single-token latency, but changed token emission patterns (larger internal KV frames) which increased page working set locality pressure. need repro with kernel backoff.

alex: action plan:
1) roll interval tweak to canary (hh-canary) now (deploy-bot triggered)
2) add extra logging in evicter for reinserts (small PR)
3) schedule microbench LRU vs FIFO with long-context traffic tomorrow (sam + alex)
4) follow-up patch for atomic reinserts (maria)

maria: I'll pick up the atomic handshake. tagging sam to help with microbench harness.

sam: got it. I'll set up FIFO/LRU perf runs and share scripts.

deploy-bot: deploy hh-canary started for config change kv.aging_sweep_interval_ms=15000 (canary=3/30 nodes). Will post status. :rocket:

alex: thanks all. logging added to the repo under `eng/runtime/evicter/logging` in the PR. will update thread with canary metrics in ~15m. :thumbsup:
